openingMessage: We win in this business by being invited back the next day. That doesn't just come from doing the job right — it comes from how we carry ourselves as professionals and as people.
openingWhy: Company men swap crew stories at every tank battery in the Basin. The crew that leaves the pad clean, calls in early, and doesn't argue gets requested by name. The one that doesn't gets replaced without a phone call. Both reputations get built one location at a time.
leadershipThought: Rescue capability must be staged before you ascend — someone must be able to get you down. That plan exists before the first rung. Not after.

specialFocus.title: Full Board Thursday: Say It Once, Say It Right
specialFocus.why:
Ray, it's a full board. More than twenty jobs, crews running three and four jobs back to back, three Davit Arm jobs below grade, and one well the board marks HIGH H2S. Keep it under ten minutes and say each point once.

Start with the intent: everyone goes home tonight, and our forms tell the truth about the day. When we point out a miss, it's to protect the crew, not to catch anybody. Wins get named out loud. Misses belong to all of us, and anything about one person's form gets handled one-on-one, not in the circle.

✓ SAY THESE NAMES
  • Michael Jobe and Hayden Haugh, Wednesday: the only two with nothing to fix all day. Trailer inspections, a full observation list, a complete Learn section, every photo from that day.
  • Robert Henigan, trailer 604 (Tue): the only readiness form that answered "anything wrong or missing?" with a plain "No." Every other form left it blank. A clear answer tells the office something. A blank tells us nothing.
  • Allen White and Dennis Easley, H2S dailies (Tue and Wed): two days running, every bottle written so anyone can read it: "6@2100psi" and "6@ 8/22." Exact, short, done.
  • Trevor McKenzie, trailer 603 (Wed): a complete readiness form, pressure and hydro date on every charged bottle: "07-25 4000."
From Matt Croom's reviews of Tuesday's and Wednesday's forms.
✎ SAY IT RIGHT TODAY: three things
  • On the form, tick what's true. Utilized means you stopped the work. Discussed means you talked about it. "Unsafe conditions" needs one sentence saying what the condition was. Yesterday, four forms ticked it with nothing unsafe written. The office reads those boxes to see where the risk is, so the box has to match the day.
  • Name the problem and the person. "Low-pressure alarm didn't sound on the cascade, told Ray at 6:15." One line like that gets a trailer fixed. A problem with nobody named can sit for days.
  • Say it back. Before the first break on every well, repeat the plan to the company man and your partner: which valve, air on, who's upwind, who calls the break. If they say "you're good," ask "good to do what?"
Ten minutes: intent (1) · names (2) · say it right (3) · rescue standard (3) · send-off (1).
specialFocus.standardLabel: Working at Height and Below Grade: Rescue Is Set Before You Start
standard: Name your rescue before you climb or go below grade: who gets you out, with what, and how long it takes.
Davit Arm jobs today (Sally E26E 105H, Sally E26A 101H, Crawford 27F 106H): the davit arm and retrieval line are set up and checked before anyone goes in.
Six feet or more, measured from where you'd land: 100% tied off. One hook is always in before the other comes off.
HIGH H2S on XBC Giddings Estate 1301H: air on, monitors on and the break plan agreed with the company man before the first line is opened.

Every well gets its own briefing and its own form. The fourth well of the day is a new location, not a copy of the first. Yesterday the same "what went well" list showed up on more than a dozen forms.
When the plan changes, say the new plan back before anyone moves.

scenarios.title: The Fourth Well
scenarios.body: It's two in the afternoon on your fourth well of the day: same crew, same company man, same job. The company man waves and says "You're good." Good to do what? The wind has turned since the morning, and the form from the first well is right there to copy. Stop and say it back: "Confirming: we break the flange on this well, air on, crew upwind, I call the break." Then fill out a fresh form for this well. Ray, ask the circle: what changed between your first well and your last one yesterday?

questions: What will you say back to the company man before your first break today?
If you go down at a Davit Arm job, who gets you out, and how long does it take?
On your last well today, what will be different from your first?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: Say it back, write it true, and name your rescue before you start. Every well gets its own briefing and its own form.
